2026-10-26.headline: Japan sends MMX towards the moons of Mars as the US Space Force signs its first commercial surveillance reserve agreements
summary: Japan launched its MMX sample-return probe towards the moons of Mars on H3 flight 10, carrying a French–German rover.
The US Space Force signed its first six operational agreements to draw on commercial space surveillance capacity in a surge.
A Russian military satellite, Kosmos 2612, made close approaches to an ICEYE radar satellite, according to a LeoLabs report released on 19 October.

Poland and Vietnam named space among the areas of a new strategic partnership, Türkiye's 2027 budget proposal nearly triples its space and aviation programme, and NASA restated a 2028 Moon landing with Artemis III as a 2027 Earth-orbit test.

Europe's ministers still meet in Rome on 15 December to decide the path for low Earth orbit, the Moon and Mars. Nothing new was decided this week. Russia's civil programmes did not move in public; the military satellite's approaches to ICEYE are the development that did.
2026-10-26.bottom_line: Japan's sample-return probe is on its way to the moons of Mars, with French and German hardware aboard, and China added another batch to its state internet constellation. The United States has now contracted commercial companies to track objects in orbit during a crisis, and NASA kept a 2028 Moon landing as its stated date while the 2027 flight stays a test in Earth orbit. Europe's next decisions are a parliamentary vote on the EU Space Act on 10 November and the ESA meeting in Rome on 15 December.

global.title: Japan launches MMX towards the moons of Mars on H3 flight 10
global.summary: An H3 rocket lifted off from Tanegashima at 04:41 Japan time on 20 October, 19:41 UTC on 19 October, carrying JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration probe. JAXA confirmed separation into a Mars transfer orbit about one hour and eleven minutes after launch. It was the tenth H3 flight and the first H3 launch of an interplanetary mission. MMX is a sample-return mission to Phobos and carries a rover built by the French and German space agencies.
global.why: It is Japan's first sample-return attempt from the Martian system and the first interplanetary mission for its H3 launcher. European and US agencies have instruments on board, so the schedule matters beyond Japan.

global.title: US Space Force signs first operational commercial reserve agreements for space surveillance
global.summary: Space Systems Command announced on 22 October the first six operational purchase agreements under the Commercial Augmentation Space Reserve, known as CASR. The agreements give the Space Force access to commercial space-domain-awareness capacity that can be called on in a surge. The Command's release does not name the companies. Press reports name Anduril, LeoLabs, Slingshot, InTrack, EOS of Australia and NorthStar of Canada.
global.why: CASR moves from concept to signed agreements, with commercial tracking capacity now contracted for wartime surge use. Two of the reported vendors are Australian and Canadian, which extends the arrangement to allied firms.

global.title: Russian military satellite Kosmos 2612 made close approaches to an ICEYE radar satellite
global.summary: A report by the tracking company LeoLabs, released on 19 October, described manoeuvres by the Russian military satellite Kosmos 2612 around ICEYE-X36 between 15 and 19 October. Reports put the closest approach at about 500 metres or less before Kosmos 2612 moved away. ICEYE is a Finnish company; ICEYE-X36 is registered in the United States and operated by its US arm. The first reports appeared on 16 and 17 October. Finland has not commented.
global.why: Close approaches by a military satellite to a commercial radar satellite bear on how states treat proximity operations in orbit. The case links a Finnish company, a US registry and a Russian military operator.

items.title: Europe's next space decisions are still the November vote and the Rome meeting
items.summary: ESA ministers meet in Rome on 15 December. In front of them is a proposal for low Earth orbit, the Moon and Mars. The October council discussed that path and did not adopt new funding. Before that, on 10 November, the European Parliament's industry committee votes on the EU Space Act, which would set rules for companies from outside the EU that serve European customers.
items.why: These two dates are when Europe either funds the plan or writes the rules. Until then, national agencies are the ones flying hardware, as France and Germany are doing on Japan's mission to the Martian moons.
items.bar: quiet desk: no claim made that needs a source

items.title: Poland and Vietnam name space among areas of a new strategic partnership
items.summary: Poland and Vietnam raised relations to a strategic partnership in Hanoi on 26 October, during a visit by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Satellite and space cooperation is among the named areas. A Polish Space Agency delegation led by its president, Marta Wachowicz, visited the Vietnam National Space Center. No contract or amount was announced for space.
items.why: The partnership puts space in a Polish framework with a South-East Asian state at head-of-government level. It gives Polish satellite firms a government channel into the Vietnamese market.

items.title: Polish Space Agency closes its watch on a Chinese rocket stage that passed over Poland
items.summary: The Polish Space Agency's space situational awareness centre tracked the second stage of a Chinese Zhuque-2E rocket, about five tonnes, on passes over Poland. In a final notice on 19 October, the agency said the stage re-entered on 18 October at about 12:33 Central European Summer Time over Borneo. A local monitoring network in Wrocław recorded a pass over Poland.
items.why: It shows Poland's national tracking service issuing public re-entry notices for foreign debris crossing its territory. Uncontrolled re-entries of large stages remain a recurring issue for states under the ground track.

items.title: Zelensky says Norway talks covered satellite communications for Ukrainian forces
items.summary: During a visit to Oslo on 20 and 21 October, President Volodymyr Zelensky met Defence Minister Tore O. Sandvik and Kongsberg chief executive Eirik Lie. Zelensky said the talks gave special attention to starting work on new satellite communications for Ukrainian forces, as an alternative to Starlink. The Norwegian government's releases on the visit do not mention satellite communications. No agreement, amount or timeline was announced.
items.why: If pursued, it would give Ukraine a European government-backed alternative for military satellite links. The claim rests on Ukraine's account; Norway has not confirmed it.

items.title: French–German Idefix rover leaves for Phobos aboard Japan's MMX
items.summary: Japan's MMX probe, launched at 19:41 UTC on 19 October, carries Idefix, a rover built jointly by the French space agency CNES and the German Aerospace Center DLR. It also carries MIRS, a French infrared spectrometer. DLR quoted German minister Dorothee Bär on the launch.
items.why: Idefix is the main French and German hardware contribution to a Japanese-led planetary mission. It ties both agencies' Mars-system science to JAXA's schedule for arrival and landing.

items.title: Italian Space Agency completes a new laser-ranging station at Matera
items.summary: The Italian Space Agency announced on 20 October the completion of MSLR, a satellite laser-ranging station working at two wavelengths at its Giuseppe Colombo Space Centre in Matera. e-GEOS built the station, with a control system from DiGOS of Potsdam. The agency cited possible future use for tracking space debris.
items.why: Laser ranging underpins precise orbits for geodesy and navigation satellites. A debris-tracking role would add a national sensor to European space surveillance.

items.title: Russia's civil space plans stayed in statements; the military satellite did move
items.summary: Roscosmos has said this month that the first module of a future Russian station is in production, and that talks with China on joint Mars hardware are under way. Those accounts come from Russian state media. What was measured, rather than announced, was a Russian military satellite, Kosmos 2612, manoeuvring close to an ICEYE radar satellite in mid-October. That episode is in the global section.
items.why: Listeners should separate a stated plan from a tracked manoeuvre. The station and the Mars talks are intentions carried by state outlets. The close approach is a recorded movement by a military satellite around a commercial one.
items.bar: quiet desk: no claim made that needs a source

items.title: Türkiye's 2027 budget proposal nearly triples the space and aviation programme
items.summary: Türkiye's 2027 central government budget justification raises the Space and Aviation programme from TL 8.73bn in 2026 to TL 24.59bn in 2027, an increase of 181.7 per cent. It plans TL 92.14bn for the programme over 2027 to 2029. The programme covers aviation as well as space; Gazete Oksijen calculates aviation at about 76 per cent of the 2027 total. The budget text gives no separate figure for space.
items.why: The increase sets the funding envelope for Türkiye's space plans for the next three years. Because aviation takes most of it, the space share cannot be read from the headline figure.

items.title: China launches the 28th group of its state low-orbit internet constellation
items.summary: A Long March 8A rocket lifted off from the Hainan commercial spaceport at 10:03 Beijing time on 25 October, 02:03 UTC, carrying the Satellite Internet Low Orbit Group 28 satellites. The China National Space Administration said the satellites reached their planned orbit. The launch came fifteen days after Group 27. All sources found are state or state-aligned media.
items.why: It keeps China's state broadband constellation on a launch rhythm of about two weeks. That pace determines how soon China can offer a national alternative to foreign low-orbit services.

items.title: NASA restates a 2028 Moon landing and sets out Artemis III as a 2027 Earth-orbit test
items.summary: NASA released an Artemis update on 23 October. It said Artemis III will launch in 2027 and send astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas, with ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano, aboard Orion into low Earth orbit to test lander operations. NASA said it and the commercial lander providers, Blue Origin and SpaceX, had streamlined their lander designs and changed their concepts of operations. Reports put Artemis III and IV at 2027 and 2028, and NASA officials restated a landing on the Moon in 2028. Administrator Jared Isaacman said NASA was exploring ways to keep Artemis III on target without compromising safety.
items.why: The update keeps a crewed landing in 2028 as NASA's stated date while the 2027 flight stays an orbital test rather than a landing. It names an ESA astronaut on the Artemis III crew and changes the lander plans of both providers.
items.bar: B: five independent sources (one government, four press); no national-language mix for a US item

items.title: NASA ends Swift science operations as the observatory's orbit decays
items.summary: NASA announced on 23 October the end of science operations for the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. Its orbit had decayed below 275 kilometres, and the final observation was made on 20 October. Re-entry is expected within weeks. A commercial reboost attempt was abandoned in August.
items.why: Swift has been a main instrument for detecting gamma-ray bursts since 2004, and its loss leaves a gap in rapid-response astronomy. Life extension by commercial reboost was not achieved for this mission.

audio_sections.title: Opening
audio_sections.text:
Good morning. It is Monday, the twenty-sixth of October, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing.

Japan has sent a probe towards the moons of Mars. The United States Space Force has signed its first operational agreements to call on commercial satellite tracking in a crisis. And a Russian military satellite's close approaches to a commercial radar satellite have been set out in detail. Europe's ministers have not taken a new decision this week. Their next one is in Rome in December.

audio_sections.title: Top story
audio_sections.text:
The top story is Japan's Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX. An H3 rocket lifted off from Tanegashima at 04:41 Japan time on Tuesday the twentieth. JAXA confirmed that the probe separated into a transfer orbit towards Mars about an hour and eleven minutes after launch. It was the tenth flight of the H3. MMX is designed to bring a sample back from Phobos, the larger of the two Martian moons. Europe has a direct stake: the probe carries a rover built jointly by the French and German space agencies.

In the United States, Space Systems Command announced on the twenty-second the first six operational purchase agreements under its Commercial Augmentation Space Reserve. These give the Space Force access to commercial space surveillance capacity that it can call on during a surge. Press reports name Anduril, LeoLabs, Slingshot, InTrack, EOS of Australia and NorthStar of Canada.

And a report by the tracking company LeoLabs, released on the nineteenth, described manoeuvres by the Russian military satellite Kosmos 2612 around ICEYE-X36, a radar satellite of the Finnish company ICEYE, between the fifteenth and the nineteenth. Reports put the closest approach at about five hundred metres or less.

audio_sections.title: ESA and EU
audio_sections.text: On the European desk, the decisions are still ahead. ESA ministers meet in Rome on the fifteenth of December, with a proposal in front of them for low Earth orbit, the Moon and Mars. The October council talked through that path and did not adopt new funding. On the tenth of November, the European Parliament's industry committee votes on the EU Space Act, the draft rules for non-European companies serving customers in the EU.

audio_sections.title: Central and Eastern Europe
audio_sections.text:
In Central and Eastern Europe, Poland and Vietnam raised their relations to a strategic partnership in Hanoi on Monday, during a visit by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Satellite and space cooperation is among the named areas. A Polish Space Agency delegation led by its president, Marta Wachowicz, visited the Vietnam National Space Center. No contract or amount was announced for space.

The Polish Space Agency also closed its watch on the second stage of a Chinese Zhuque-2E rocket, about five tonnes, which passed over Poland. Its final notice, issued on the nineteenth, said the stage re-entered on the eighteenth over Borneo.

audio_sections.title: Nordics
audio_sections.text: On the Nordic desk, President Volodymyr Zelensky met Norway's Defence Minister, Tore Sandvik, and the head of Kongsberg, Eirik Lie, during his visit to Oslo on the twentieth and twenty-first. Zelensky said the talks gave special attention to new satellite communications for Ukrainian forces, as an alternative to Starlink. That account comes from the Ukrainian side. The Norwegian government's releases on the visit do not mention satellite communications, and no agreement, amount or timeline was announced.

audio_sections.title: Western and Southern Europe
audio_sections.text:
In Western and Southern Europe, the French and German share of MMX is Idefix, a rover built jointly by the French space agency CNES and the German Aerospace Center, DLR. The probe also carries a French infrared spectrometer. DLR quoted German minister Dorothee Bär on the launch.

In Italy, the Italian Space Agency announced on the twentieth that it had completed a new satellite laser-ranging station at its space centre in Matera. The station was built by e-GEOS. The agency said it could later be used to track space debris.

audio_sections.title: Eurasia and Central Asia
audio_sections.text: On the Eurasia desk, Russia's civil announcements this month have been statements: the first module of a future Russian station is said to be in production, and talks with China on joint Mars hardware are said to be under way. Those accounts come through Russian state media. The development that was tracked, rather than announced, was a Russian military satellite manoeuvring close to a commercial ICEYE radar satellite in mid-October.

audio_sections.title: Türkiye, Middle East and Africa
audio_sections.text: On the Türkiye, Middle East and Africa desk, Türkiye's 2027 budget proposal raises the Space and Aviation programme from 8.73 billion lira this year to 24.59 billion lira next year, an increase of almost 182 per cent. The programme covers aviation as well as space, and the budget text gives no separate figure for space.

audio_sections.title: Asia Pacific
audio_sections.text: In Asia Pacific, besides the MMX launch, China launched the twenty-eighth group of its state low-orbit internet satellites. A Long March 8A rocket lifted off from the Hainan commercial spaceport on Sunday at 10:03 Beijing time. The China National Space Administration said the satellites reached their planned orbit. This came fifteen days after the previous group. The account of the launch comes from Chinese state media.

audio_sections.title: Americas
audio_sections.text:
In the Americas, besides the Space Force agreements, NASA released an Artemis update on the twenty-third. Artemis III is to launch in 2027 as a test in low Earth orbit, with astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas, and the European Space Agency's Luca Parmitano, aboard Orion. NASA said it and the two lander providers, Blue Origin and SpaceX, had streamlined their lander designs. Officials restated a landing on the Moon in 2028.

Also on the twenty-third, NASA announced the end of science operations for the Swift Observatory, after its orbit decayed. Re-entry is expected within weeks.

audio_sections.title: Close
audio_sections.text: Looking ahead, the Asia-Pacific Regional Space Agency Forum opens in Thailand tomorrow, and the United Kingdom's Defence in Space Conference also opens tomorrow. The first of two spacewalks to install new solar arrays on the International Space Station is planned for Thursday. The European Parliament's industry committee votes on the EU Space Act on the tenth of November, and ESA ministers meet in Rome on the fifteenth of December. The next monthly edition is on Tuesday the third of November. That is the briefing for Monday the twenty-sixth of October.

In Brussels, the European Parliament's industry committee is set to vote on the EU Space Act on November tenth.
In Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi agreed on Thursday to deepen cooperation in defense, space and nuclear energy, and to double trade by twenty thirty.
Today the delegation visits Bengaluru, home of the Indian space agency, where a cooperation agreement between the two space agencies is planned.
Also in Poland, the satellite maker Creotech plans a new factory by twenty twenty nine that could build up to a hundred satellites a year, about ten times today's output.
Its chief executive warned that Europe will depend on American rockets for years to come.

He said Poland is still interested in Artemis, but its lunar priority is Europe's Argonaut lander.
In Türkiye, Industry Minister Mehmet Fatih Kacır said the country plans to send its lunar vehicle in the first months of twenty twenty seven.
He added that work has started on a spaceport in Somalia, which he said could cut launch costs by about thirty percent.
In Uzbekistan, the space agency is reaching out to African countries ahead of the International Astronautical Congress in Samarkand in October twenty twenty eight.
It has proposed an easier visa route for delegates.
In Hungary, Polish space officials and companies held talks in Budapest with the Hungarian space industry and the HUNOR astronaut program.
They covered secure satellite communications under IRIS², a bigger role for both countries in ESA programs, and the EU's next long term budget.
Czechia, Sweden and Greece had no major new space news overnight, though Greece and Czechia both have dates coming up in the days ahead.
On the business side, Blue Origin has asked federal regulators to allow up to fifty New Glenn launches a year from Florida.
That's more than four times the current limit of twelve, and it comes five months after a New Glenn exploded on its pad.
Written comments are open until October thirtieth.
Looking ahead, NASA's Artemis update is this afternoon.
Next week brings the Von Braun Symposium in Huntsville from Monday, and two conferences on Tuesday and Wednesday, one in Toulouse on space resilience and one in London on defense in space.
On October twenty ninth, astronauts on the space station begin the first of two spacewalks to install new solar arrays, with the second set for November fifth.
Greece's public call to name its first astronaut mission closes on October thirtieth.
Czech Space Week runs from November second to the eighth.
The United States votes in its midterm elections on November third.
That's the briefing for today.
You'll find the full edition, with links to every source, on the Briefing tab.
Have a good day.

2026-10-23.bottom_line: Governments are moving from buying access to building national capability, and the decisions that shape Europe's commercial LEO market cluster in the next eight weeks: NASA station proposals on December 8 and ESA's Rome meeting on December 15. ESA is keeping several providers in play, with a Vast MoU and a Crew Dragon concept already on the table, so offers that bring industrial participation and a funding path will count for more than seats.

items.summary: At their October 22 summit in New Delhi, Prime Ministers Modi and Tusk agreed to deepen cooperation in defense, space and nuclear energy, aim to double trade by 2030 and launch a V4 plus India format. The delegation, including POLSA, Scanway, ICEYE and Polish ESA project astronaut Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski, visits Bengaluru on October 23, where a POLSA and ISRO cooperation agreement is planned.
items.title: Modi and Tusk agree to deepen space and defense ties, Bengaluru stop today
items.why: Poland is building space partners outside Europe and the United States, and its Ax-4 astronaut shares a flight history with India's Shubhanshu Shukla.

sources.title: Polish satellite maker Creotech Instruments plans tenfold capacity boost by 2029

items.summary: Polish satellite maker Creotech Instruments plans a factory in Mazowieckie by 2029 able to build 40 mixed satellites or 100 of one model a year, against about 10 today, and will open French and German subsidiaries within weeks. Its CEO said Europe will rely on US rockets for years and that launch access is becoming a lever of political pressure.
items.title: Creotech plans tenfold satellite output and warns on US launch dependence
items.why: Polish industry is scaling fast and thinking in sovereignty terms, which makes it a candidate supplier in a regional supply chain integration model.

sources.title: US political uncertainty complicates long-term Artemis commitments, Polish minister says

items.summary: In a written reply dated October 13 to a question from MP Adrian Zandberg, reported on October 19, Deputy Minister Michał Jaros cited high costs, limited access for outside partners, no transparency on NASA's financing and US budget uncertainty. He said Poland remains interested in Artemis but its lunar priority is ESA's Argonaut lander.
items.title: Polish deputy minister questions Artemis terms and names Argonaut as the lunar priority
items.why: Warsaw is signaling that it wants demonstrable industrial return from US-led programs, not that it is walking away from them.

sources.title: Polska i Węgry rozmawiają o bezpiecznej łączności satelitarnej

Topics were secure satellite communications under IRIS², a larger role for both countries in ESA programs and the EU's 2028 to 2034 budget. No agreement was reported.

segments.text: Good morning.
It's Thursday, October twenty second, and here's what's happening in space.
Europe's space agency has wrapped up its council meeting in Paris with a plan for low Earth orbit, the Moon and Mars headed to ministers in Rome.
A Polish executive has been named to run the agency's commercial partnerships.
And Türkiye's new budget nearly triples its space and aviation program.
The European Space Agency's three hundred and fiftieth council met in Paris on Wednesday and Thursday.
Member states discussed a proposal from Director General Josef Aschbacher on Europe's future in space exploration.
It sets out a path that can grow step by step, from low Earth orbit to the Moon and then Mars, pairing more European autonomy with international cooperation.
That matters because the International Space Station is heading toward retirement, and Europe still hasn't decided what replaces its presence in orbit.
Delegates also confirmed that the intermediate ministerial meeting will take place in Rome on December fifteenth.
Early preparatory work can start within existing budgets.
The council also reviewed relations with the European Union, including the next seven year E-U budget, the European Competitiveness Fund and the E-U Space Act.
The agency asked for a clear split of roles with Brussels, so that the two don't duplicate work.
In the United States, NASA holds an Artemis briefing at Kennedy Space Center on Friday afternoon.
Administrator Jared Isaacman and program managers will cover Artemis three, now a crewed test in Earth orbit next year, and the goal of landing astronauts on the Moon in twenty twenty eight.
In Washington, senators are pressing SpaceX and the Pentagon over speed limits placed on Starlink terminals used by Ukrainian forces earlier this month.
And the State Department has launched Project Constellation, a five million dollar, two year effort to build space ties with more than seventy emerging space nations.
In India, the space agency has cleared a key separation test for the Gaganyaan crew capsule.
The uncrewed first flight, carrying the robot Vyommitra, is still promised for this year, with a crewed flight targeted for twenty twenty seven.
Brussels and Washington are at odds over satellite spectrum.
The European Commission is preparing to reserve part of the two gigahertz band for direct to device service by European operators.
The American ambassador to the E-U has warned of severe retaliation if non-European constellations are shut out.
The dispute feeds a wider European debate about sovereign access to space.
It also lands as the E-U Space Act moves toward a committee vote in the European Parliament on November tenth.
In Poland, ESA's council named Andrzej Banasiak, who runs Safran Electronics and Defense in Poland, as the agency's Director of Commercialisation and Industry Partnership.
He starts on January first.

At the same time, Prime Minister Donald Tusk is in India with about a hundred business leaders, including the Polish space agency, the companies Scanway and ICEYE, and astronaut Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski.
A cooperation agreement between the Polish space agency and India's space agency is planned during the trip, and the delegation heads to Bengaluru on Friday.
In Hungary, the science and technology ministry, which now oversees space, says police have opened investigations into four of its complaints about earlier government contracts.
The same ministry is reviewing inherited space contracts worth roughly eight hundred and twenty to eight hundred and fifty billion forints, some running to twenty forty.
In Türkiye, the twenty twenty seven budget bill raises the space and aviation program to about twenty four point six billion lira, up from eight point seven billion this year.
Close to ninety two billion lira is planned over three years, with the country's first lunar spacecraft aiming for launch in twenty twenty seven.
There was no major new space news today from Uzbekistan, Czechia, Sweden or Greece.
On the business side, SpaceX and Tesla have each set up board committees to study a possible merger, after SpaceX reported revenue of about fourteen point six billion dollars for the quarter.
Rocket Lab says its Neutron rocket won't fly until twenty twenty seven, after flaws turned up in the composite domes of its fuel tanks.
Xona Space Systems raised two hundred and fifty million dollars to build a commercial navigation constellation of about two hundred and fifty eight satellites.
And Hewlett Packard Enterprise plans to send an A-I computer to the Moon on an Astrolab rover, testing language models and image processing on the lunar surface.
Looking ahead, NASA's Artemis briefing is on Friday, October twenty third, the same day the Polish delegation visits Bengaluru.
Novaspace's space summit in Toulouse and the Defence in Space conference in London both run on October twenty seventh and twenty eighth.
Astronauts on the space station are set to make the first of two spacewalks to install new solar arrays on October twenty ninth, with the second on November fifth.
Greece's mission naming call closes October thirtieth.
Americans vote in the midterm elections on November third.
And the European Parliament's industry committee is scheduled to vote on the E-U Space Act on November tenth.
That's the briefing for today.
You'll find the full edition, with links to every source, on the Briefing tab.
Have a good day.

items.summary: The ESA Council appointed Andrzej Banasiak, managing director of Safran Electronics and Defense in Poland, as Director of Commercialisation and Industry Partnership from January 1, 2027, based at ECSAT in Harwell. Polish officials welcomed it as a gain for national standing in Europe, noting Poland's pledge of nearly EUR 550 million to ESA optional programs for 2026 to 2028.
items.title: Pole named ESA director for commercialization and industry
items.why: Poland now holds the ESA post that manages commercial partnerships, investors and member state industry links, which raises its weight in shaping commercial LEO models.

A POLSA and ISRO cooperation agreement is planned during the visit, with the delegation due in Bengaluru on October 23.
items.title: Tusk takes POLSA and Polish space firms to India
items.why: Warsaw is widening its space partners beyond ESA and the US, giving India a channel into Polish industry and its astronaut heritage.

items.summary: The 2027 central government budget bill allocates about TRY 24.6 billion to the space and aviation development program, up from TRY 8.7 billion in 2026, rising to TRY 37 billion by 2029 and about TRY 92 billion over three years. The line covers space and aviation together, and reporting on the budget justification puts about TRY 18.7 billion of the 2027 amount, roughly three quarters, in air transport facilities, so the space share is not broken out. The bill still has to pass parliament.
items.title: Türkiye's 2027 budget bill nearly triples a combined space and aviation line, mostly for aviation
items.why: The headline figure overstates space spending, but the three year line still gives the lunar program and agency projects a funded home if they are written into the justification.

sources.title: Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger is a good idea as companies form deal committees

global.summary: Elon Musk said a combination of SpaceX and Tesla would be a good idea and confirmed both boards have set up independent committees to study it, with no terms agreed. The news followed SpaceX third quarter results showing revenue up 161 percent to $14.58 billion, more than half of it from AI data center leasing.
global.title: SpaceX and Tesla form committees to weigh a merger
global.why: A larger, cash-rich SpaceX deepens government dependence on one provider for crew transport and connectivity, which shapes how ministries view station and transport risk.

sources.title: Congress Seeks Answers On Starlink Disruptions in Ukraine

global.summary: Speed restrictions on Starlink terminals used by Ukrainian forces between October 12 and 14 drew a letter from four Democratic senators to SpaceX and a bipartisan request from nine senators for a Pentagon inspector general review. Musk said the Starshield changes reflected US government decisions.
global.title: Senators press SpaceX and the Pentagon over Starlink limits in Ukraine
global.why: European capitals will cite the episode as proof that sovereign access matters, which colors how they judge any US-led space partnership.

sources.title: State Department Taps Trio for $5M Space Diplomacy Push

global.summary: The US Mission in Vienna announced Project Constellation, a two-year, $5 million effort led by Meridian International Center with the Commercial Space Federation and SPACEAIMS. It targets more than 70 aspiring space nations with exchanges, delegation visits and training, and aims to align their positions at COPUOS.
global.title: State Department launches $5 million space diplomacy program for emerging nations
global.why: It creates a US-funded channel for capacity building and commercial matchmaking in emerging space nations where China and Russia also compete for partners.

global.summary: NASA leadership briefs on Artemis at Kennedy Space Center on October 23 under the title Artemis Acceleration, with Artemis III now a 2027 Earth orbit docking test and a crewed landing still planned for 2028. A National Academies report released October 21 ranks Bhabha Crater, Mons Hadley, Orientale Basin and Aristarchus Plateau as the top non-polar sites for short crewed sorties.
global.title: NASA Artemis update due Friday as lunar landing site debate opens
global.why: Any Artemis slip or reshaping changes how partner governments weigh lunar commitments against nearer-term LEO presence.

sources.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise to Send AI Compute Module to the Moon

global.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise will fly its fourth Spaceborne Computer on Astrolab's FLIP rover, testing language models, LiDAR and imagery processing and autonomous monitoring on the lunar surface, with NASA and Deloitte running workloads. It is the first unit in the series designed to operate in vacuum, with launch expected in 2026.
global.title: HPE to fly an AI computing module on a lunar rover
global.why: Edge computing beyond Earth is moving from demonstration to product, which raises the bar for how orbital computing offers are framed to governments.

items.title: ISRO clears Gaganyaan module separation test ahead of uncrewed G1

items.title: Rocket Lab pushes Neutron debut into 2027

items.title: Xona raises $250 million for a commercial GPS constellation

segments.text: Good morning.
It's Wednesday, October twenty first, and here's what's happening in space.
Uzbekistan has signed the Artemis Accords.
NASA has set the rules for its commercial space station competition.
And Europe's space agency is meeting in Paris, with a big ministerial decision coming in December.
Uzbekistan became the seventy seventh country to sign the Artemis Accords.

sources.title: Uzbekistan, US sign Artemis Accords on exploration of Moon, Mars, comets and asteroids
Artemis Accords
Uzbekistan, US hold first Enhanced Strategic Partnership Dialogue

items.summary: Uzbekistan signed the Artemis Accords in Samarkand on October 19, following talks between Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov and Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the first bilateral Enhanced Strategic Partnership Dialogue. Saidov said the step widens cooperation with NASA, including training national specialists and transferring space technologies.
items.title: Uzbekistan joins the Artemis Accords as 77th signatory
items.why: The signature gives the government commission a politically anchored US option for its human spaceflight decision.

sources.title: Uzbekistan, United States sign 54 agreements worth $12 billion
Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the U.S.-Uzbekistan Business and Investment Council

items.summary: During the Rubio visit, US and Uzbek parties signed 54 agreements worth about $12 billion across critical minerals, finance, aviation, rail, healthcare and digital technology. Amazon Leo will work on satellite communications, and GE Aerospace will supply engines for new Uzbekistan Airways aircraft.
items.title: US and Uzbekistan sign 54 deals worth $12 billion, including satellite communications
items.why: US commercial presence in Tashkent is now broad enough to carry an industrial participation package attached to a spaceflight offer.

sources.title: Uzbekistan and China to Expand Cooperation on AI and Digital Economy
Uzbekistan proposes SCO-2040 strategy and new security coordination mechanism

items.summary: On October 21 Uzbekistan announced expanded AI and digital economy cooperation with China and signed a healthcare roadmap with Russia, a day after proposing an SCO-2040 strategy. The government also announced free AI computing access for startups and universities.
items.title: Tashkent keeps China and Russia tracks running in parallel
items.why: Tashkent is hedging across partners, so a US-aligned offer has to win on ecosystem value, not alignment alone.

sources.title: Polska i Węgry rozmawiają o bezpiecznej łączności satelitarnej

items.summary: Polish Space Agency, Polish interior ministry and Polish industry representatives met Hungarian space industry and HUNOR program representatives in Budapest around October 16 to discuss IRIS2 secure communications, deeper ESA participation and the 2028 to 2034 EU budget. POLSA also presented Poland's regional role at the CEE Space and Defense Day conference in Hungary.
items.title: POLSA delegation in Budapest opens Poland-Hungary track on secure satcom and ESA
items.why: A working Poland-Hungary channel on ESA and EU programs is a practical base for V4 industrial cooperation.

sources.title: US political uncertainty complicates long-term Artemis commitments, Polish minister says

items.summary: In a written reply to a parliamentary question on POLSA's limited role in NASA programs, Deputy Minister of Development and Technology Michał Jaros said Artemis financing lacks transparency and NASA-run programs are costly with limited partner access. He said Poland will keep working closely with ESA and named the Argonaut lunar lander as its lunar priority.
items.title: Polish deputy minister questions Artemis costs, names ESA Argonaut as lunar priority
items.why: Warsaw's supervising ministry is signaling an ESA-first posture, so US-linked offers to Poland need an explicit industrial return story.

sources.title: Blue Origin rozwija działalność w Polsce

items.summary: Blue Origin registered Blue Origin Poland II on September 28 and Blue Origin Poland on October 8, both in Kraków, with job postings for ASIC design, embedded systems and software tied to its TeraWave constellation. One posting targets a 2027 tape-out for a high-throughput modem and digital beamforming chip.
items.title: Blue Origin opens two Polish entities in Kraków for satellite chip work
items.why: A rival station developer is building a Polish engineering footprint it can cite in any Polish partnership conversation.

sources.title: SSC Space and ArkEdge Space sign SSC Space Go and ground segment contract
SSC Space and ElevationSpace sign MoU to explore cooperation

items.summary: SSC Space signed an SSC Space Go and ground segment contract with ArkEdge Space on October 20, four days after an MoU with ElevationSpace to explore cooperation. Both partners are Japanese space startups.
items.title: SSC adds two Japanese partners in a week

sources.title: Προτείνετέ μας το όνομα της αποστολής του πρώτου Έλληνα αστροναύτη!
ESA signs agreement with Vast for first Greek astronaut mission
ESA and Vast expand mission collaborations for the post-ISS era

items.summary: The Hellenic Space Center and the Ministry of Digital Governance opened a public call, closing October 30, to name the Vast-PAM-1 mission that will fly ESA project astronaut Adrianos Golemis to the ISS for two weeks in summer 2027. The seat comes through ESA's September 9 agreement with Vast, and the same flight carries France's Thomas Pesquet and Czechia's Aleš Svoboda.
items.title: Greece launches naming call for first astronaut's Vast-PAM-1 flight
items.why: Greece's first flight is contracted with a competitor, so the opportunity shifts to follow-on missions and station utilization.

sources.title: Fergani'nin altıncı uydusu FRG-100D4 başarıyla yörüngesine yerleşti

items.summary: Fergani's FRG-100D4, a 160 kg satellite with domestically developed avionics, reached a 590 km orbit after launch on SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 rideshare on October 20. It tests navigation and broadband payloads for the planned Uluğ Bey constellation, which targets more than 200 satellites within five years.
items.title: Baykar-linked Fergani puts sixth test satellite in orbit
items.why: Türkiye's private sector is building sovereign navigation and communications capacity quickly, which raises the bar for what a station partnership must add for Ankara.

sources.title: NASA Issues Final RFP for Commercial Space Stations in LEO After ISS Retirement
NASA szuka prywatnego następcy ISS
NASA

global.summary: NASA's final commercial LEO destinations solicitation, issued October 9, sets proposals due December 8 and awards around April 15, 2027 to two or more firms on firm fixed price contracts with a $100 million guaranteed minimum and a $34.06 billion ceiling over up to 15 years. A NASA official said on October 19 that the agency should cut requirements on participants further.
global.title: NASA commercial station competition terms fixed, lighter requirements signaled
global.why: Demonstrated international demand, including sovereign partner commitments, is one of the clearest ways to evidence the commercial viability NASA says it will judge.

sources.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch
Felmerült az egyesülés lehetősége a SpaceX-nél és a Teslánál, Musk támogatná

global.summary: SpaceX reported third quarter revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161 percent year on year, and net income of $4.4 billion, with launch contributing $1.8 billion and Starlink and AI segments most of the rest. Elon Musk said Starship Flight 15, targeted for November, will attempt to catch both stages, and both SpaceX and Tesla have formed shareholder committees to study a combination.
global.title: SpaceX posts $14.6 billion quarter, plans double Starship catch
global.why: SpaceX cash generation and Starship cadence set the cost and schedule benchmark for every commercial station and crew transport plan.

sources.title: When will SpaceX and Blue Origin fly to the Moon? NASA reveals lunar lander timelines and an Artemis III update
NASA potwierdza. Osłona termiczna statku Orion zdała egzamin
NASA Update on Artemis Program

global.summary: NASA's updated plan keeps Artemis III as a mid-2027 Earth orbit test of Orion docking with SpaceX and Blue Origin lander test articles, with the first crewed landing on Artemis IV in early 2028. Post-flight analysis found the Orion heat shield performed as expected on Artemis II, with nine small char loss areas against 103 on Artemis I, and NASA leadership briefs on the program October 23.
global.title: Artemis lander timelines firm up, Orion heat shield cleared
global.why: Artemis schedule credibility shapes how Accords signatories weigh NASA-led lunar participation against ESA options.

sources.title: 500 méterre közelített meg egy orosz műhold egy Ukrajnának fontos műholdat
Mit művelt az orosz műhold?

global.summary: Russia's Kosmos 2612 matched orbits with Iceye-X36, a commercial radar satellite owned by Iceye's US subsidiary, and closed to roughly 500 meters around October 16 before moving away by October 19. Analysts tie it to a pattern of Russian approaches to Iceye satellites since May, whose imagery has supported Ukraine since 2022.
global.title: Russian satellite shadows commercial radar satellite used for Ukraine
global.why: Counterspace behavior against commercial assets strengthens the security case inside sovereign space programs across CEE and the Nordics.

2026-10-21.headline: Uzbekistan signs the Artemis Accords in Samarkand, giving its pending astronaut decision a US-aligned political frame

profile_updates.change: Signed the Artemis Accords in Samarkand on October 19, 2026 as the 77th signatory.
Adrianos Golemis assigned to Vast's first private ISS mission in summer 2027 under an ESA contract with Vast.

sources.title: Media invitation: information session following the 350th ESA Council
ESA Selects Airbus and OHB to Lead European Space Station Studies

items.summary: ESA's 350th Council meets at headquarters in Paris on October 21 and 22, with Director General Josef Aschbacher briefing media on October 22 ahead of the December 15 Intermediate Ministerial Meeting in Rome. Proposals for Rome include a European-led LEO station option now under parallel feasibility studies by Airbus and OHB consortia, with initial development capped at €1 billion per three-year funding period.
items.title: ESA Council meets in Paris ahead of Rome ministerial
items.why: Rome decides whether Europe buys commercial station access, contributes to one, or builds its own, which frames every ESA member state seat and payload conversation.

sources.title: Space Rider Test Model Lost Following Failed Drop Test

items.summary: The full-scale Space Rider test model was lost when its parafoil failed to deploy during the final drop test campaign, the second interruption this year, and an independent investigation is underway. ESA still expects a first flight in 2028 but has moved the target from the first to the second quarter.
items.title: Space Rider test model lost in failed drop test
items.why: Europe's own reusable microgravity return capability slips again, which keeps European researchers dependent on partner platforms.

sources.title: Megvan az aláírás: jöhet az európai műholdas internet, nagy nevek dolgozhatnak rajta
Mobilní operátoři

items.summary: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica and Vodafone signed a letter of intent to reserve spectrum and jointly provide ground infrastructure for a European satellite internet service, with the constellation partner still unselected. The effort sits alongside the EU's IRIS2 program, and no formal link has been stated.
items.title: Four European telecom groups sign intent on sovereign satellite service
items.why: Sovereignty arguments are now driving private European procurement as well as public programs.

sources.title: French MPs propose symbolic €1 budget line for VORTEX spaceplane

items.summary: French members of parliament proposed a symbolic one euro budget line for the VORTEX spaceplane during the budget debate. The move keeps a national reusable vehicle option visible while ESA debates Europe's post-ISS human spaceflight path.
items.title: French lawmakers propose token budget line for VORTEX spaceplane

sources.title: Španělsko schválilo předčasné financování špionážních družic PAZ 2

items.summary: Spain approved early release of funds for the PAZ 2 radar reconnaissance satellites. It is another European government accelerating sovereign defense space spending.
items.title: Spain fast-tracks funding for PAZ 2 reconnaissance satellites

sources.title: 'Enduring partners of choice'. Central Asian nations, US agree to expand ties at Samarkand meeting
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Uzbekistan Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov at the C5+1 Ministerial

items.summary: Foreign ministers of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan met Secretary Rubio in Samarkand on October 19 and issued a joint statement on trade routes, critical minerals, energy, security and trusted technology. The statement does not mention space.
items.title: C5+1 ministers in Samarkand frame the US as a long-term regional partner
items.why: US political attention to Central Asia makes Kazakhstan and its neighbors plausible next Artemis Accords candidates and opens room for US-aligned human spaceflight offers.

sources.title: Velitelství Vesmírných sil

items.summary: Reporting indicates the US Space Force component in the Middle East may expand to five times its current size. It signals a heavier US military space footprint in the Gulf region.
items.title: US Space Force Middle East command may grow fivefold

sources.title: MMX lifts off to Mars's moon Phobos
JAXA's MMX Enroute to Mars To Return Samples of Phobos
Japanese MMX mission launches to study Martian moons

items.summary: JAXA launched the MMX mission on the first H3-24L from Tanegashima on October 19 UTC, carrying the French and German Idefix rover and NASA instruments, with Phobos samples due back in 2031. ESA supplied deep space communication equipment and Estrack ground station support under its Science Program.
items.title: Japan launches MMX Phobos sample return with European support

sources.title: Blue Origin plánuje na Floridě obří expanzi
What's Happening in Space Policy October 18-24, 2026

items.summary: Blue Origin plans additional Florida launch pads, a manufacturing expansion and more recovery vessels to increase the New Glenn flight rate. The FAA holds a public meeting on October 22 on its draft environmental assessment for more Blue Origin launches at Cape Canaveral.
items.title: Blue Origin plans new Florida pads to raise New Glenn cadence
items.why: Higher New Glenn cadence matters for Orbital Reef and Blue Moon schedules, both competitors for the same post-ISS and lunar budgets.

government.notes: Space policy is decided at presidential level by decree and executed by GGPEN under MINTTICS, with an interministerial commission coordinating ministries. Funding comes from the state budget approved by the National Assembly, historically combined with export credit and intergovernmental financing for satellites from Russia and France. The government announced in October 2025 that GGPEN will be converted into an Angolan Space Agency, but formal creation was not confirmed in this run. President Lourenço is in his final term, and the next general election is expected in 2027.

strategy.summary: Angola's National Space Strategy 2016-2025 was approved by Presidential Decree No. 85/17 and is implemented by GGPEN, the national space program management office under the telecommunications ministry. It is built on five axes: space infrastructure, training and promotion, industry and technology, international positioning, and organization and cooperation. Its horizon has passed and no successor strategy was found, though the government cited it in October 2025 when announcing the conversion of GGPEN into an Angolan Space Agency.

strategy.title: Plan Espacial Nacional 2016-2027 (preliminary version); successor roadmap: Bases para el Desarrollo Espacial Argentino (10 Dec 2025)
strategy.status: preliminary (approved by the CONAE Directorio and presented to the executive; no adopted successor found)
strategy.owner: CONAE (proposes and executes the plan); Directorio of CONAE; presented to the national executive; the Bases were presented by the SICyT
strategy.summary: The official CONAE page describes the Plan Espacial Nacional as a strategic plan, a state policy of national priority, with three components: Earth observation, peaceful exploration and use of outer space, and technological development for space use. The preliminary version 2016-2027 was approved by the CONAE Directorio and presented to the national executive (CONAE page, 2026). On 10 Dec 2025 the SICyT presented the Bases para el Desarrollo Espacial Argentino as a roadmap for a new plan, including a national space hub, a space-access project and an astronaut-training platform, and international value-chain integration. The full bases document was not found on the official site.
strategy.budget: No consolidated budget for the plan is published in the sources opened. Decree of Necessity and Urgency 867/2026, published in the Boletín Oficial on Friday 4 Sep 2026 (regional press, La Capital), increased CONAE resources for programmes and activities linked to space policy; the press report gives no amount. A press-reported real-terms cut of about 65 percent since December 2023 was not verified and is not used.
goals: Earth observation for Argentina's continental and maritime territory (CONAE plan axis)
Peaceful exploration and use of outer space, including cooperative missions (CONAE plan axis)
Technological development for space use and domestic industry (CONAE plan axis)
strategy.law: No comprehensive national space activities law was found. Ley 27208 (Ley de Desarrollo de la Industria Satelital; sanctioned 4 Nov 2015; Boletín Oficial 11 Nov 2015) declares the development of the satellite industry a matter of national interest and state policy (art. 1) and approves the Plan Satelital Geoestacionario Argentino 2015-2035 (art. 2). A 'Ley Espacial Argentina' bill appeared only in a search snippet; its PDF was not readable and it is not used.

strategy.owner: Government of the Republic of Armenia; authorised state body under Law HO-152-N (not named)
strategy.summary: No standalone national space strategy document was found. The Prime Minister said on 10 Sep 2026 that the Government Programme 2026–2031 makes national space capabilities a standalone strategic objective. The stated goals are at least three national satellites (two Earth observation, one telecommunications), sovereign ground infrastructure, a distributed ground-station network and participation in international programmes. The legal basis is Law HO-152-N on Space Activity (6 Mar 2020), which sets Government approval of development and financing programmes and a Government-authorised state body. A science-sector programme 2026–2030 names space as a priority (PM release; not fetched).
strategy.budget: No space budget line or consolidated national space budget found in the fetched sources. The law finances space activity from the state budget (Art. 9). Budget figures in the seed (AMD 10 million licensing duty; tax incentives to 2030) are not re-proved and are excluded.
goals: Operate at least three national satellites: two Earth observation, one telecommunications (PM release, 10 Sep 2026)
Build sovereign ground-based infrastructure and domestic capacity for satellite command, control, data reception and processing (PM release, 10 Sep 2026)
Establish a distributed network of ground stations for national and international missions (PM release, 10 Sep 2026)
Enable Armenian engineers and companies to contribute to international space programmes (PM release, 10 Sep 2026)
strategy.law: Law of the Republic of Armenia on Space Activity, No. HO-152-N, adopted 6 Mar 2020 by the National Assembly, published 1 Apr 2020 (ARLIS), in force 11 Apr 2020 (ARLIS header and UNEP LEAP). Government decrees on licensing (No. 1984-N), registration and alienation of space objects are listed in UN document A/AC.105/C.2/2025/CRP.6; their texts were not read in this pass.

strategy.summary: The Statement on Space, released in July 2026 by the Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science, sets the federal government's vision for lifting national space industrial capability, moving into higher value work and expanding into global markets. It identifies five focus areas and the levers government can use to coordinate demand, investment and regulation. The Australian Space Agency is consulting industry, academia and government on detailed actions expected later in 2026. It sits alongside the earlier Australian Civil Space Strategy 2019 to 2028 and a new Statement of Expectations to the agency.

strategy.title: Space Strategy 2030
strategy.owner: Azercosmos (Space Agency of the Republic of Azerbaijan)
strategy.summary: Space Strategy 2030 is published on the Space Agency website as the sector development path to 2030. Its three goals are economic growth and sustainable space development, a national space ecosystem based on research, and national interest through space projects. Priority directions include satellite service sustainability with replacement satellites, local production with a Spacecraft Development Center and at least 50 jobs, national security and backup links, and research, human capital, startups and SMEs. The strategy has no stated budget. Its predecessor is the 2009 State Programme on the Establishment and Development of the Space Industry.
strategy.budget: No budget for Space Strategy 2030 found in any fetched official source. Cabinet decision No. 106 (16 Apr 2026) changes a figure in clause 5.1 of the agency charter from 473 605 880 to 567 605 880; currency and purpose are not stated in the extracted text, so it is not recorded as a strategy budget. The seed USD 120 million satellite purchase (2023 press) is not re-proved.
goals: Ensuring economic growth and sustainable development in space
Formation of a national space ecosystem based on scientific research and application of innovative solutions
Protecting national interests by implementing space projects for peace and prosperity
Priority: sustainability of existing satellite services, including replacement of satellites at end of orbital life
Priority: local production potential, a Spacecraft Development Center with at least 50 jobs
Priority: national security use of satellites and backup links for strategic infrastructure
Priority: expansion of space research and human capital; startups and SMEs

government.notes: Space is a federal competence led by the Minister for Science Policy, with BELSPO preparing ESA subscriptions and managing programs. Large ESA packages are decided by the Council of Ministers, and in December 2025 the government added defense co-financing so that part of space spending counts toward NATO targets. Regional governments fund economic support for industry, and the balanced regional distribution of industrial return is an explicit consideration in federal decisions. Defence now runs its own satellite procurement, starting with the GALO constellation.

Belgium contributed EUR 296 million to ESA in 2024. Defence announced a military observation constellation (GALO) costing over EUR 200 million in July 2026.

Keep the ESA ESEC site in Redu as the ESA and EU cybersecurity reference center
Increase Belgian staff and a Belgian director post at ESA
Complete a strategic review of Belgian space policy by 2028 considering economic return and regional balance

strategy.summary: Belgium has no single published long-term national space strategy document. Federal space policy is set through the Council of Ministers decision of 23 December 2025 on Belgian space programming for 2026 to 2030, which funded the ESA subscriptions made at the November 2025 Bremen ministerial and introduced defense co-financing of ESA participation. BELSPO designs and implements the policy around science, societal use, industrial development and economic return. The decision mandates a strategic review by 2028 to define future Belgian space policy.

Space activity rests on the SPARRSO statute (Act 29 of 1991), the state owned Bangladesh Satellite-1 communications satellite operated by Bangladesh Satellite Company Limited, and the Artemis Accords, which Bangladesh signed in April 2025. government.notes: Bulgaria has no space agency and no space law, so space policy runs through the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation (renamed from Innovation and Growth when the Radev government took office on 8 May 2026), which manages ESA cooperation under the ECS Agreement and PECS calls, with major commitments approved by the Council of Ministers. Research funding flows through the Ministry of Education and Science and the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, while defense space sits with the Ministry of Defence. A presidential election is scheduled for 25 October 2026 with a possible runoff on 1 November 2026, and President Iotova (in office since 23 January 2026 after Rumen Radev resigned) is a candidate, with the current term ending 22 January 2027.

strategy.summary: Bulgaria has no adopted national space strategy. In its 2025 statements to UN COPUOS the government said drafting a National Space Strategy and a National Space Program is its top short-term priority, alongside domestic space legislation and the creation of a national space agency. A draft update to the Innovation Strategy for Smart Specialisation 2021-2027 adds a national priority on space and dual-use technologies (public consultation closed 20 September 2026).

government.notes: Chile has no space agency. Policy is set by the Ministry of Science through a presidential advisory commission, while most operational capability and spending sit with the Ministry of Defense and the Air Force through the National Satellite System. Funding flows through ministry lines in the annual Budget Law approved by Congress. President Kast took office on March 11, 2026, for the 2026-2030 term, and his March 2026 cabinet named Ximena Lincolao as Minister of Science and Fernando Barros as Minister of Defense.

strategy.summary: Chile's National Space Policy was approved by Supreme Decree No. 30 of July 2024 and cleared by the Comptroller General in March 2025, succeeding the 2014-2020 policy. It rests on two central objectives, the sustainable development of national space capabilities and the integrated management of space for national security and socioeconomic progress, organized around six strategic axes. Implementation runs largely through the National Satellite System (SNSat) operated by the Chilean Air Force and the National Space Center in Cerrillos, which opened in December 2025.

strategy.summary: White paper issued by the State Council Information Office in January 2022 that reviews progress since 2016 and sets out space tasks for the following five years under the long-term aim of building China into a space power. It covers launch vehicles, space infrastructure, human spaceflight, lunar and planetary exploration, space governance and international cooperation. No successor space white paper was found in this run, and current direction is carried forward by the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026 to 2030) adopted in March 2026, which shifts space toward a market-oriented industry with large constellations, reusable launchers and crewed lunar preparations.

strategy.summary: No national space strategy, space policy or space programme document was found. The Council of Ministers adopted on 4 June 2025 a decree on the creation, powers, organisation and operation of ASCI, a public administrative establishment of a scientific and technological nature whose fields are Earth observation, space weather, astronomy, space exploration, and satellite navigation and communications. The national development plan PND 2026-2030 is the only national planning document opened that mentions space, and only via satellite data for AI-enabled resource use.

strategy.summary: Colombia's most recent adopted space policy is CONPES 3983 of January 2020, which set enabling conditions for the space sector to support national productivity and competitiveness, with an action plan that closed in December 2021. It called for reforming the Colombian Space Commission, reducing barriers for private entry, filing orbit and spectrum resources with the ITU, and commercializing defense satellite capabilities. As of 2025 the Colombian Space Commission reported to UN COPUOS that it was drafting a new National Space Policy to define national space governance and institutions, and no successor policy had been identified as adopted by this date.

Law 9960, Art. 13 sets funding sources: a five-year contribution from non-financial public institutions (excluding central government, municipalities, CCSS, ICE, public universities and UTN), own revenue, and donations or credits. MICITT with Finance must produce financial studies within one year (Transitorio VII).

strategy.budget: In August 2025 the Ministry of Transport proposed raising annual ESA contributions by 345 million koruna (220 million for optional programs and 125 million for the ESA framework project for Czechia), with the Ministry of Defence adding 320 million koruna a year from 2026 for defense space topics. The government earmarked 2 billion koruna over three years for the Czech astronaut mission (Resolution No. 365 of 21 May 2025). The plan sets a minimum ESA funding level in an annex not reviewed here, and no figure for the 2025 ESA Ministerial Council subscription was confirmed.
goals: Build a complete chain to design, build, operate and use small satellites, and advance to large subsystems, instruments and end-to-end solutions
Use satellite data and services across economic sectors, including security and defense
Maintain and expand strategic partnerships with international partners
Develop an education and outreach ecosystem for space sector talent
Strengthen research teams able to lead national and international science missions as principal investigators
Make state institutions a key customer for Czech space technologies and maintain national space and ground infrastructure
Secure adequate funding, institutional anchoring and staff for managing space activities
strategy.law: No national space law in force. Legal commentary in 2024 noted that Czech law still lacks a framework for activities in outer space, and no government draft act was found in this run.

strategy.summary: Approved by the government in October 2025, the plan sets the long-term vision for Czechia as an active and internationally recognized space actor that uses space technologies for the economy, society and security. It defines seven strategic goals and seven competence platforms, from satellites up to 500 kg and scientific instruments to Earth observation data processing and space security and defense. It also frames the national Czech Path to Space project, including a Czech astronaut mission to the ISS expected around 2027 to 2028. Coordination of space activities moved from the Ministry of Transport to the Ministry of Industry and Trade on 1 March 2026.

strategy.summary: Germany's national space strategy was adopted by the federal cabinet on 27 September 2023, replacing the 2010 strategy, and treats space infrastructure as critical infrastructure for Germany and Europe. It sets nine fields of action ranging from European and international cooperation and New Space growth to security, sustainability, research and exploration. Since 2025 federal civil space policy has been consolidated in the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), which told the Bundestag in November 2025 that a decision on rewriting the strategy will follow once its new space department is fully established. A separate Space Security Strategy was presented in cabinet in November 2025.

government.notes: Civil space policy is led by the research ministry, which on 3 June 2026 merged with the digitalization ministry into the Ministry of Research, Education and Digitalization under Christina Egelund. Funding is set through Folketing political agreements and Finance Acts, most recently the November 2025 agreement of DKK 2.7 billion for 2026 to 2029, and flows mainly to ESA subscriptions and national research programs. The Ministry of Defence pursues space for Arctic surveillance and communications on a separate track. The government formed after the 24 March 2026 election is a minority coalition of the Social Democrats, Green Left, Moderates and Social Liberals.

strategy.budget: A November 2025 political agreement set aside DKK 2.7 billion for space from 2026 to 2029, described by the ministry as the largest Danish public space investment ever. Denmark committed about DKK 1.1 billion to ESA voluntary programs for 2026 to 2028 at the November 2025 Ministerial Council, and DKK 400 million goes to a strategic space program under Innovation Fund Denmark.
goals: Strengthen Danish space research and innovation environments
Double voluntary ESA contributions from DKK 280 million to DKK 580 million by 2035
Develop four national space missions over ten years, led by the Máni lunar mission
Use space to support defense, security and preparedness, including Danish satellites and Arctic coverage
Build a domestic market for space-based solutions and commercialize Danish space research
Expand international partnerships and participation in EU space programs and Horizon Europe
strategy.law: The Outer Space Act (Lov om aktiviteter i det ydre rum, Act No. 409 of 2016) governs licensing and supervision of space activities, registration of space objects and liability, administered by the ministry responsible for research.

strategy.summary: Presented by the government on 18 November 2024, the ten-year strategy aims to strengthen Denmark's position in ESA, address climate and environmental challenges, support defense, security and preparedness, and grow innovative companies. It sets out nine initiatives, including a national space program for research and innovation, a program of four national space missions with a Danish-led lunar mission (Máni) as flagship, and a goal to double voluntary ESA contributions by 2035. A November 2025 political agreement then allocated DKK 2.7 billion to space for 2026 to 2029.

government.notes: Presidential republic: the President is both head of state and head of government. No national space agency, space office, space strategy, space budget or space law was found. A 2022 CESAC communique said a space agency was being created with a council of ministries and agencies; no decree or law creating it was found, and a 2026 press item says the agency is still only proposed. On 27 Feb 2026 the President announced a commercial spaceport in Oviedo, Pedernales with a US firm (named LOD Holdings in the transcript); the 2028 readiness date comes from a 2 Mar 2026 press report, not from the transcript. The Presidency is marked lead:true because it is the only body with a proven role in the current project; this is lead by practice, not by a legal mandate. The Presidency ministries page still lists MEPyD; the ministry site now shows Ministerio de Hacienda y Economía after the 2025 merger (Law 45-25 per press). Gaceta Oficial and the Chamber of Deputies portal were unreachable.

government.notes: Space decisions in Egypt are concentrated at the presidential level, with the President appointing EgSA's CEO (one-year renewable terms) and board by decree. The Prime Minister chairs the EgSA board, which brings in the higher education, communications and other ministries. The current CEO, Majed Ismail, was appointed by Presidential Decree No. 439 of 2025.

strategy.summary: Spain has no single adopted national space strategy. Its civil space policy rests on the Spanish Space Agency (AEE), created by Royal Decree 158/2023 under the joint authority of the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities and the Ministry of Defense, and on the 2022 Aerospace PERTE investment plan. strategy.summary: Ethiopia's Space Policy was approved by the Council of Ministers on 22 December 2018 to guide all national space activities toward peaceful, development-oriented uses. It structures the sector into civil and defense and security tracks, makes government the lead funder, and assigns implementation and permitting to the national space institute. strategy.summary: Adopted by government resolution on 30 December 2024 and published in 2025, the strategy replaces the 2018 national space strategy and aims to make Finland the most advanced space operating environment by 2030. It calls for growth of the space sector, identification of capabilities in which Finland wants to be self-sufficient, and international cooperation to supplement them, with emphasis on security and dual-use technology. Measures are carried out within existing budgets of the administrative branches, and the Finnish Space Committee monitors implementation.

strategy.title: Ghana Space Policy
strategy.horizon: No end year stated. The policy's implementation matrix sets timelines from 1 year to 5 years.
strategy.owner: Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation (MESTI); implementation by GSSTI and GAEC
strategy.summary: The policy sets a national framework for space science and technology (SST): establishing a Ghana Space Agency, space education, infrastructure, research, applications and commercialisation, international collaboration, a legal and regulatory framework, and outreach. It was approved by Cabinet in March 2022 and unveiled in November 2024. It states the policy 'will be coordinated by' MESTI.
strategy.budget: No appropriated amount found. Policy target: 'Allocate at least 0.1% of GDP for SST activities', with annual budget support for the national space agency and an SST development fund (policy Section 5, Financing; Ministry of Finance named as the responsible body in the implementation matrix).
goals: Establish the Ghana Space Agency as a national entity with legal authority
Space education and human resource development
Build space infrastructure, including ground stations and research centres
Promote space science research and development
Space application and commercialisation of space products
Collaboration with relevant local and international organisations
Legal and regulatory framework, including ratification of the five UN outer space treaties

strategy.summary: Greece presented its first National Space Strategy, running to 2030, together with the HELLAS-SPACE 2.0 program at the Greece in Orbit event on 26 June 2026. The strategy follows the first phase national microsatellite program funded through the Recovery and Resilience Facility and ESA, and shifts emphasis from participation in European programs to domestic production and technological autonomy. It sets five national goals and includes a governance system with annual progress reviews. HELLAS-SPACE 2.0 targets national production lines and international tenders with at least 50 percent Greek participation.

strategy.summary: Indonesia's space policy rests on Law No. 21 of 2013 on Space Activities and the 2017 presidential master plan that sets long term targets to 2040 for space science, remote sensing, space technology, launch and commercial space activities. Since the former space agency LAPAN was merged into the National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN) in 2021, space research and implementation sit inside BRIN. The master plan is evaluated every five years, and BRIN officials stated in early 2026 that some targets need to be redefined to be more adaptive and realistic. Current priorities are a national spaceport at Biak, Papua, and domestically built Earth observation satellites focused on food security.

strategy.summary: Cabinet-approved policy that opens the full space value chain to non-government entities and assigns distinct roles to the Department of Space, ISRO, IN-SPACe and NSIL. government.notes: Strategic direction rests with the Supreme Leader, while the civil program is set by the Supreme Space Council under the President and run by the ICT ministry through ISA and ISRC. Funding comes through the annual budget law approved by the Majlis and through defense channels for the IRGC track, which operates largely outside civil oversight. Mojtaba Khamenei was named Supreme Leader on 8 March 2026 after Ali Khamenei was killed on 28 February, and he has not appeared in verified video or audio since, so his health and role are disputed. The war that began in February 2026 is unresolved as of this date, with a US naval blockade and intermittent strikes, which adds uncertainty to budgets and leadership.

strategy.summary: Iran's space activity is governed by a 10-year roadmap drafted by the ICT ministry and approved by the Supreme Space Council in 2022, which aims to make Iran a regional hub for space technology. Priorities are Earth observation, communications and positioning satellites, sovereign launch capability, and reaching geostationary orbit. The program has continued during the 2026 war despite strikes on facilities, including the Iranian Space Research Center in Tehran. A civil track under the Iranian Space Agency runs in parallel with a military track under the IRGC Aerospace Force.

strategy.summary: Approved at the 29th COMINT meeting on 14 May 2026, the DSPSN is Italy's first comprehensive national planning framework for space and implements the Government Guidelines on Space and Aerospace approved by COMINT in late 2024. It sets priorities for the next decade along four axes: research and benefits for society, industrial competitiveness, governance and regulation, and international cooperation. It treats space as a domain of strategic competition and calls for a national space security strategy, a critical space technologies plan and operational security and defense capabilities. It operates within Law No. 89 of 2025 on the space economy.

strategy.budget: The Space Strategy Fund at JAXA targets about 1 trillion yen over ten years, with 0.8 trillion yen secured as of 2025 (Cabinet Office, 2026). JAXA's annual budget was 215.5 billion yen in fiscal 2023.
goals: Ensure space security, including space domain awareness and resilient satellite systems
Strengthen national resilience and address global issues through Earth observation, positioning and communications
Create new knowledge through space science and exploration, including Artemis lunar participation
Strengthen the industrial and technology base, including H3 launch capability
Double the space industry market from 4.0 trillion yen (2020) to 8.0 trillion yen in the early 2030s
Expand the QZSS regional navigation constellation to seven and later eleven satellites
strategy.horizon: 10 year plan with a 20 year outlook, roadmap revised annually
strategy.law: The Basic Space Act (2008) is the framework law. The Space Activities Act (2016) licenses launches and satellite control, and the Diet passed an amendment in June 2026 that extends licensing to rocket launches generally, adds pre launch certification of space objects and broadens operator liability, with human spaceflight and reusable vehicles left to later rules. The Remote Sensing Data Act (2016) and the Space Resources Act (2021) are also in force.

strategy.summary: The 4th Basic Plan, decided by the National Space Committee on 21 December 2022, covers 2023 to 2027 and frames the goal of becoming a major space economy power by 2045. It is implemented through annual plans by the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA), founded in May 2024 under the Ministry of Science and ICT. A July 2026 National Space Committee meeting accelerated lunar lander timelines and set a domestic LEO communications network target for 2035. The next five-year basic plan is due to cover the period from 2028.

strategy.summary: Luxembourg's national space strategy for 2023 to 2027 is set by the Ministry of the Economy and implemented by the Luxembourg Space Agency (LSA). Its central theme is sustainability, organized around economic sustainability, sustainability of activities on Earth and in space, and the responsible use of space resources. It aims to grow and diversify the space sector as part of the national economy, backed by ESA participation, the national LuxIMPULSE program, and dedicated finance instruments. The strategy horizon ends in 2027, so a successor document is due.
